title: Plan J: AI Data Analysis / Research Report
summary: Define the question → clean data → exploratory analysis → deep modeling → visualize & narrate → conclusions
scenario: Best for business dashboards, user analysis, competitor research and paper data — from a question to a decision-ready conclusion.

steps.title: Define the question and metrics
steps.detail: Turn a vague ask into a quantifiable question and metrics (definition, time range, comparison group). Ambiguity in scope is the #1 analysis killer — align on what you're measuring first.
steps.tips: Write 'the question + which metrics + where data comes from' and let the AI check what's missing.

steps.title: Clean the data
steps.detail: Handle missing values, outliers, duplicates, types and formats. Have the AI write cleaning scripts and output before/after stats.
steps.tips: Inspect distributions (describe / value_counts) before deciding how to treat missing values — don't blindly drop rows.

steps.title: Exploratory analysis
steps.detail: Look at distributions, correlations, group comparisons and trends; let the AI generate charts to surface patterns. This step yields the 'leads worth digging into'.
steps.tips: Correlation ≠ causation; describe the phenomenon first, then design a validation.

steps.title: Deep modeling
steps.detail: Pick the method for the question (regression / clustering / significance test / prediction), split train/test, check metrics and watch for overfitting. Have the AI write the model code and explain the result.
steps.tips: Don't throw a complex model at a small sample; run a simple baseline first and add complexity gradually.

steps.title: Visualize and narrate
steps.detail: Use KPI cards plus clear charts to tell what happened, why, and what it means. Keep axes and palette consistent to avoid misleading visuals.
steps.tips: Start axes at zero, label units and sample sizes; every chart needs a one-line takeaway, not silence.

steps.title: Conclusions and recommendations
steps.detail: Package findings as 'conclusion + evidence + recommendation + limitations', stating assumptions and data limits explicitly.
steps.tips: Stating limitations and confidence beats overselling — it reads more credible, not less.

pitfalls.title: Poor data quality
pitfalls.detail: Dirty data yields beautiful but wrong conclusions; cleaning and QA are the most important step.

pitfalls.title: Confusing correlation with causation
pitfalls.detail: Correlation is not causation; distinguish 'observed association' from 'verified cause' in the report.

pitfalls.title: Overfitting / tiny samples
pitfalls.detail: Complex models on small data give irreproducible results; use simple baselines plus cross-validation.

pitfalls.title: Misleading charts
pitfalls.detail: Truncated axes, unlabeled units, missing sample sizes all mislead; visualize to spec.
